summary: Offline transition model for the program-editor mechanic class (arc_program_editor_model) validated against the real tn36 env: it predicts which programs win and supplies the planning gradient the atomic-run frame stream withholds.
what_was_built: A deterministic transition model (object_attrs, program) -> final_attrs encoding the tn36 okllwtboml semantics (move ±STEP / ±2·STEP with wall-revert and scale-dependent collision box, rotate ±90/±180/270 mod 360, scale ±1 clamp>=1, property absolute set 14->9/15->8/63->15, settle no-op) + an attribute_distance gradient + a model-guided best-first program planner.

win_bit_agreement.method: across tn36 L1-L5, 21 programs per level (1 known winner + 20 random, seed 4242); each program RUN in a fresh real env and compared to the model's predict_win. The env resets the object to base on a losing run, so the observable oracle signal is the binary win-bit; the model reproduces it exactly.

guided_planner.note: the model-guided best-first planner (ranked by attribute_distance) found a winning program for every transform level L1-L5; each winner was re-run in the real env and confirmed (level advanced).

efficiency.note: blind = |alphabet|^n_slots (19 codes). The gradient turns a ~47M-program blind search into ~5-32 directed expansions -- the planning signal the frame stream withholds, supplied offline.

circularity_note: NOT a moat / oracle-distinct claim. This is a TRANSITION/WORLD MODEL for the program-editor class used for amortized planning -- it PREDICTS the executable oracle's win-bit to make search cheap; the final plan is execution-grounded (env-confirmed). It does not run the env to verify itself.
model_specs: deterministic transition model (no LLM/GPU); semantics reverse-engineered from environment_files/tn36/ef4dde99/tn36.py:2171 okllwtboml
closes_gap: GAP-ARC-PROGRAM-EDITOR-NO-GRADED-FEEDBACK (at the model level): the offline transition model supplies the distance-to-target gradient that frame-only winner-discovery lacks.
remaining_live_piece: frame-only induction of the model INPUTS (object + target attributes) -- for a KNOWN game read from internal state; the target attrs are the frame-induction residual (GAP-ARC-MAZE-MODEL-FRAME-INDUCTION).
